subject: Invoice submission: Brightstream Health — portal vs email / template questions
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@brightstreamhealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: accounts-payable@brightstreamhealth.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Brightstream billing / invoice template and preferred delivery

Hi Vivek / Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're completing Brightstream's onboarding and want to align on the invoice delivery path. Our AP team (cc'd) currently sends invoices as PDF attachments by email and names files like BRIGHTSTREAM_INV_####.pdf. I've attached our current invoice template (Brightstream_invoice_template_v2.xlsx) for reference.

Two quick questions:
- Do you prefer that we upload invoices to Redwood's vendor portal, or is emailing PDF attachments acceptable as a long-term flow?
- If email is okay, do you require a specific filename convention (PO in filename, vendor id, etc.) or any field we must include in the PDF itself?

We can make small format changes if it speeds go-live. Hoping for guidance so we can finalize our AP export.

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Director, Finance Operations
Brightstream Health
attachments: Brightstream_invoice_template_v2.xlsx

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@brightstreamhealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightstream billing / invoice template and preferred delivery

Hi Sarah — thanks for sending the template. A few recommendations from procurement/ops to keep the onboarding smooth:

1) Portal-first preference: Our standard recommendation is vendor portal upload (one invoice per upload) because it gives automated PO matching, richer acknowledgements, and faster payment SLA tracking. If your ERP can push to SFTP or our portal connector we'll get idempotency and better ledger mapping.

2) Email fallback allowed: If the portal isn't possible right away, email PDF is acceptable as a fallback. For email-based delivery please follow these minimal conventions so our ingestion doesn't need manual intervention:
   - Filename: BRIGHTSTREAM_PO{PO_NUMBER}_INV{INVOICE_NUMBER}.pdf (PO must be present in filename).
   - One invoice per PDF (no multi-invoice combined PDFs).
   - PDF should include a clear PO number and an invoice total line matching the filename.
   - Ideally include a single-line CSV attachment with line items when invoices have >1 PO or multi-line distribution (we can parse CSVs automatically).

3) Fields to add to your template:
   - PO number (separate field, not in the description column)
   - Tax amount as a separate line
   - Supplier remit address block (we use this for entity mapping)

I've uploaded a short mapping doc to the onboarding drive that shows the fields we map during intake: https://redwood.app/drive/onboarding/BRIGHTSTREAM (see "invoice-mapping.xlsx").

If you can update the filename convention and confirm you will emit one PDF per invoice, we can proceed with an expedited sandbox test. If Brightstream cannot change export naming, we can do a temporary manual parse and then discuss an exception (we'd need SLAs). Jordan — can you run the exception review if needed?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Procurement (Vendor Onboarding)
Redwood Inference

Hi Vivek — thanks for the clear checklist. A few quick clarifications from our AP team:

- We can update the filename to include the PO number (we'll emit BRIGHTSTREAM_PO{PO}_INV{INV}.pdf).
- Most of our invoices are single-PDF per invoice; a minority are combined (we'll split those).
- We don't currently export a separate CSV for line items from our accounting system, but we can include line items in the PDF in a tabular section — is that sufficient?

Attached is an example PDF export from our system (Brightstream_sample_invoice.pdf). We plan to push the updated naming convention next week. If you still need a temporary manual exception while we finish the change, please advise the acceptance window and any extra data you need.

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
